title: Patente vocabulary
_note: patente-vocab run, 2026-11-15: words written by hand for Italy, not yet checked by a second reader. Vocabulary only: no official exam questions and no text from any manual. translations.en = English meaning; deHint = German translation (the 'German' tab). All words are own entries (no refs into the lexicon, which is still being converted). Terms in flux (foglio rosa / practice authorisation, test format, prices) are deliberately left out.
intro: Start with the group you need, from the parts of the car to what your instructor says. This deck is vocabulary only: it has no exam questions, it doesn't replace a driving school or the official material of the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport, and it won't prepare you for the exam on its own.
introEasy: Do you want to drive in Italy? Learn the words for the car, the road, the exam and the papers here.
tipps: Learn both words. Everyday speech and official papers often differ: la macchina and l'autovettura, la gomma and il pneumatico, la freccia and l'indicatore di direzione.
Instructors usually say tu (gira a destra). An examiner may use Lei: giri a destra, vada dritto, si fermi qui. It means the same.
Say the instructions out loud while you sit in a parked car, or as a passenger. You will hear them faster when you are at the wheel.
